text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm seeing an attribution hole when keys created via the token-exchange path hit the routing layer. Console shows "Unattributed" and quotas aren't being charged properly. Anyone else seen this?
aj: Saw the same yesterday in prod. Billing flagged an inconsistency. Quick triage: the proxy swap seems to strip project claim for some service-account flows.
leo: Ugh. Is this the infamous projectless SA case where the console intentionally hides keys?
maya: Yep — keys that end up without a project claim are filtered in the console and then the telemetry pipeline drops the metric, so quota attribution is missing.
sam: Can we fallback to org-level attribution for meter/quotas? That would at least surface charge in billing.
aj: Security caution: some customers rely on project-level isolation. Falling back to org could misattribute cost to a different billing leaf.
maya: Fair. Proposed short-term mitigation: tag events with "org_fallback=true" in telemetry and show "Org fallback (needs audit)" in the console instead of hiding. That keeps visibility and avoids silent under/over charging.
leo: Implementation note: authn-proxy should preserve original_sa_id and emit an X-Orig-Project header before token-exchange mutates claims. Small code change:
```
// authn-proxy excerpt
req.headers['x-original-project'] = claims.project_id || ''
proxy.forward(req)
```
aj: Also add a pipeline rule that never drops metrics for missing project claims — just map them to org fallback bucket with proper tag.
maya: I'll draft an RFC for the longer-term design, but we need a quick detection + dashboard now. Can someone add an alert for spikes in missing-project_claim events?
deploy-bot: Alert rule created: auth.missing_project_claim_rate > 5/min => notify #eng-oncall. (rule id: alert-5072)
sam: We should also add a small UI hint in the console explaining "why this key is org-attributed" — reduce support tickets.
leo: Tests: add e2e that simulates token-exchange proxying and validates telemetry shows org_fallback tag and console row with explanation.
aj: I'll take tests and pipeline change. maya, can you own the console note + RFC?
maya: Yep. I'll open tickets: ENG-14210 (RFC + migration plan), ENG-14211 (console hint), ENG-14212 (dashboard + alert remediation). I'll also add a short playbook for support to explain billing artifacts to customers.
sam: One more: Dedicated customers might need opt-out or strict mode where missing-project claim results in request rejection. Add a config flag.
maya: Good call — add to RFC.
leo: Thanks — good triage. :thumbsup:
